notes: Zero-build embed: a single <pre class="mermaid"> block with erDiagram text. An agent can CRUD the diagram by editing that text block in the HTML file directly — no toolchain, trivially git-diffable, renders client-side.

Text-first DSL with an explicit ER-diagram shape and notably nicer default themes/layout than Mermaid per multiple 2026 diagram-as-code roundups. Compile step (d2 CLI, a Go binary) produces a static SVG to drop into an HTML page — agent edits the .d2 text, re-runs the CLI, commits the SVG.

The long-standing lowest-common-denominator renderer many Python ERD tools (erdantic, ERAlchemy) target. Agent-CRUD is fine at the .dot text level, but default aesthetics are dated and node/edge editing at scale is verbose compared to purpose-built ERD DSLs.

Usable outside a React build via a bundled script tag, but it's a React component library at heart — expect friction embedding in a plain-HTML page without a bundler. Included for completeness since the user asked about html/ specifically.

Unifies Mermaid, D2, PlantUML, GraphViz, DBML, and a dedicated 'Erd' diagram type behind one HTTP API — an agent CRUDs the diagram by editing the source text, then the page just embeds an whose URL/body encodes that text (deflate+base64 for GET, or POST). Zero client-side JS required, which makes it the lowest-friction option for a static HTML page.
